title: So too, bhikkhus, for one who walks in what is not his own domain, in another's territory. Therefore, bhikkhus, do not walk in what is…
content: So too, bhikkhus, for one who walks in what is not his own domain, in another's territory. Therefore, bhikkhus, do not walk in what is not your own domain, in another's territory. Bhikkhus, walking in what is not your own domain, in another's territory, Māra gains an opportunity, Māra gains an object. And what, bhikkhus, is not a bhikkhu's own domain, what is another's territory? It is the five strands of sensual pleasure. What five? There are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. There are sounds cognizable by the ear ... odors cognizable by the nose ... tastes cognizable by the tongue ... tangibles cognizable by the body that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. Bhikkhus, this is not a bhikkhu's own domain, this is another's territory. Bhikkhus, walk in your own domain, in the territory of your parents. Bhikkhus, walking in your own domain, in the territory of your parents, Māra does not gain an opportunity, Māra does not gain an object. And what, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu's own domain, what is the territory of his parents? It is the four foundations of mindfulness. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body ... feelings as feelings ... mind as mind ... phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and displeasure in regard to the world. This, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu's own domain, the territory of his parents.

title: Elder Ramaṇīyavihāri: Like a good thoroughbred, well-trained, of good breed, Having stumbled, stands up again, steady. I possess right view, a disciple of the Perfectly…
content:
Elder Ramaṇīyavihāri:

Like a good thoroughbred, well-trained, of good breed,
Having stumbled, stands up again, steady.
I possess right view, a disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One.

title: Both in the past and now, Sajjha, I have said: 'A bhikkhu who is an Arahant, with taints destroyed, accomplished, done what had to be…
content: Both in the past and now, Sajjha, I have said: 'A bhikkhu who is an Arahant, with taints destroyed, accomplished, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, attained the goal, destroyed the fetter of existence, rightly liberated — he cannot transgress nine things: A bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot intentionally deprive a living being of life; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot take what is not given, that is, stealing; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot engage in sexual intercourse; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot knowingly speak falsely; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot enjoy sensual pleasures from stored-up goods as he did when he was a householder. A bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot reject the Buddha; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot reject the Dhamma; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot reject the Saṅgha; a bhikkhu with taints destroyed cannot reject the training.'

title: Bhikkhus, this is my instruction to you. All conditioned things are impermanent. Strive on with diligence for your own liberation. Before long, the Tathāgata will…
content: Bhikkhus, this is my instruction to you. All conditioned things are impermanent. Strive on with diligence for your own liberation. Before long, the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna. Three months from today, the Tathāgata will attain final Nibbāna.

title: Poṭṭhapāda, I teach the Dhamma for the abandonment of the gross self-identification. If you practice accordingly, then defiled states will be abandoned, pure states will…
content: Poṭṭhapāda, I teach the Dhamma for the abandonment of the gross self-identification. If you practice accordingly, then defiled states will be abandoned, pure states will increase, and you will personally realize, attain, and abide in the here and now with full and extensive wisdom. Poṭṭhapāda, it is possible that you might think: 'Defiled states will be abandoned, pure states will increase, and one will personally realize, attain, and abide in the here and now with full and extensive wisdom, yet suffering still remains.' Poṭṭhapāda, do not think thus. When defiled states are abandoned and pure states increase, one in this very life, with direct knowledge, attains and abides in full and extensive wisdom, then joy arises, gladness, tranquility, mindfulness, clear comprehension, and a pleasant abiding arise.

title: Elder Devasabha (II): Accomplished in right striving, practicing on the foundations of mindfulness, Filled with the flower of liberation, he will attain cessation, taintless.
content:
Elder Devasabha (II):

Accomplished in right striving, practicing on the foundations of mindfulness,
Filled with the flower of liberation, he will attain cessation, taintless.

title: Bhikkhus, there are these six impossible cases. What six? A person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the Teacher; a…
content: Bhikkhus, there are these six impossible cases. What six? A person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the Teacher; a person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the good Dhamma; a person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the Saṅgha; a person possessed of right view cannot live without reverence and deference toward the training; a person possessed of right view cannot revert to what should not be reverted to; a person possessed of right view cannot bring about an eighth state of existence. Bhikkhus, these are the six impossible cases.

title: One who is restrained in body, speech, and mind, Who does no evil deeds, Whose three doors are guarded, Him I call a brahmin. One…
content:
One who is restrained in body, speech, and mind,
Who does no evil deeds,
Whose three doors are guarded,
Him I call a brahmin.

One from whom one can learn the good Dhamma
Taught by the Perfectly Enlightened One,
One should venerate that person,
As a brahmin venerates the sacrificial fire.

One is not a brahmin because of matted hair,
Nor because of family or birth.
One in whom there is truth and Dhamma,
Who is pure — that one is a brahmin.

title: - Bhikkhus, one who delights in the earth element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Bhikkhus,…
content: - Bhikkhus, one who delights in the earth element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering. Bhikkhus, one who delights in the water element ... one who delights in the fire element ... one who delights in the air element delights in suffering. One who delights in suffering, I say, is not freed from suffering.

title: A framework of sinews and bone, plastered with flesh and skin, The body is covered by a skin — it is not seen as it…
content:
A framework of sinews and bone, plastered with flesh and skin,
The body is covered by a skin — it is not seen as it really is.

Filled with a full belly: the liver, bladder, heart, lungs,
Kidneys and spleen, mucus, saliva, sweat, fat, blood, synovial fluid,
Bile, and serum.

From these nine streams, defilement constantly flows:
From the eyes, eye discharge; from the ears, ear discharge;
From the nose, nasal mucus; from the mouth, sometimes vomit,
Bile and phlegm; from the body, sweat and dirt.
